purpose.statement: MainProgram is an interactive, menu-driven Account Management System that continuously presents the user with options to view a balance, credit an account, debit an account, or exit, delegating all account operations to a called sub-program named 'Operations'.

code_references.snippet:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. MainProgram.

MAIN-LOGIC.
           PERFORM UNTIL CONTINUE-FLAG = 'NO'
               DISPLAY "Account Management System"
               ...
           END-PERFORM
           DISPLAY "Exiting the program. Goodbye!"
           STOP RUN.

business_rules.statement: The main menu loop continues to execute repeatedly until the user explicitly chooses to exit (option 4), at which point the CONTINUE-FLAG is set to 'NO' and the loop terminates.

code_references.snippet:
PERFORM UNTIL CONTINUE-FLAG = 'NO'
               ...
               WHEN 4
                   MOVE 'NO' TO CONTINUE-FLAG
               ...
           END-PERFORM

business_rules.statement: User choice 1 (View Balance) invokes the 'Operations' sub-program with the operation code 'TOTAL ', representing a balance inquiry.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '

business_rules.statement: User choice 2 (Credit Account) invokes the 'Operations' sub-program with the operation code 'CREDIT', representing a credit transaction against the account.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'

business_rules.statement: User choice 3 (Debit Account) invokes the 'Operations' sub-program with the operation code 'DEBIT ', representing a debit transaction against the account.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '

business_rules.statement: User choice 4 (Exit) sets the continuation flag to 'NO', causing the menu loop to terminate gracefully after the current iteration completes.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 4
                       MOVE 'NO' TO CONTINUE-FLAG

business_rules.statement: Any user input outside the valid range of 1 through 4 is treated as invalid; the program displays an error message and re-presents the menu without performing any account operation.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN OTHER
                       DISPLAY "Invalid choice, please select 1-4."

business_rules.statement: The valid user-choice values are constrained to a single digit (PIC 9), meaning only numeric values 0–9 can be accepted from the terminal; non-numeric input behaviour is governed by the runtime environment.

code_references.snippet: 01  USER-CHOICE       PIC 9 VALUE 0.

inputs.statement: USER-CHOICE is a single-digit numeric working-storage field populated interactively at runtime via an ACCEPT statement from the system console/terminal; it drives all menu routing logic.

code_references.snippet: 01  USER-CHOICE       PIC 9 VALUE 0.
ACCEPT USER-CHOICE

outputs.statement: All menu text, prompts, the invalid-choice error message, and the exit farewell message are written to the standard system display (console/terminal) via DISPLAY statements.

code_references.snippet:
DISPLAY "--------------------------------"
               DISPLAY "Account Management System"
               DISPLAY "1. View Balance"
               DISPLAY "2. Credit Account"
               DISPLAY "3. Debit Account"
               DISPLAY "4. Exit"
               DISPLAY "--------------------------------"
               DISPLAY "Enter your choice (1-4): "
DISPLAY "Exiting the program. Goodbye!"

outputs.statement: Account state changes (balance, credits, debits) are produced as outputs by the called 'Operations' sub-program; MainProgram itself does not write account data directly.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '
                   WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'
                   WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '

processing_logic.statement: Initialization: CONTINUE-FLAG is pre-set to 'YES' and USER-CHOICE to 0 in working storage before the PROCEDURE DIVISION begins execution, establishing the loop entry condition.

code_references.snippet:
01  USER-CHOICE       PIC 9 VALUE 0.
       01  CONTINUE-FLAG     PIC X(3) VALUE 'YES'.

processing_logic.statement: Menu Display: At the start of each loop iteration, a bordered menu listing the four available options is displayed to the terminal.

code_references.snippet:
DISPLAY "--------------------------------"
               DISPLAY "Account Management System"
               DISPLAY "1. View Balance"
               DISPLAY "2. Credit Account"
               DISPLAY "3. Debit Account"
               DISPLAY "4. Exit"
               DISPLAY "--------------------------------"
               DISPLAY "Enter your choice (1-4): "

processing_logic.statement: User Input Acceptance: The program pauses and accepts a single-digit numeric value from the user into USER-CHOICE.

code_references.snippet: ACCEPT USER-CHOICE

processing_logic.statement: Menu Routing (EVALUATE): The accepted USER-CHOICE is evaluated; matching values 1, 2, or 3 result in a CALL to 'Operations' with the corresponding operation code; value 4 sets CONTINUE-FLAG to 'NO'; any other value triggers an invalid-input message.

code_references.snippet:
EVALUATE USER-CHOICE
                   WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '
                   WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'
                   WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '
                   WHEN 4
                       MOVE 'NO' TO CONTINUE-FLAG
                   WHEN OTHER
                       DISPLAY "Invalid choice, please select 1-4."
               END-EVALUATE

processing_logic.statement: Loop Condition Check: After each iteration's EVALUATE block, the PERFORM UNTIL condition re-tests CONTINUE-FLAG; if it equals 'NO' the loop exits, otherwise the menu is displayed again.

code_references.snippet: PERFORM UNTIL CONTINUE-FLAG = 'NO'

processing_logic.statement: Termination: Once the loop exits, a farewell message is displayed and STOP RUN is issued, terminating the program and returning control to the operating system.

code_references.snippet:
DISPLAY "Exiting the program. Goodbye!"
           STOP RUN.

dependencies.statement: External sub-program 'Operations': MainProgram has a hard dependency on a separately compiled COBOL sub-program named 'Operations'. It is called dynamically (CALL literal) with a 6-character alphanumeric operation code ('TOTAL ', 'CREDIT', or 'DEBIT ') passed BY REFERENCE. This sub-program must be link-edited or dynamically loadable at runtime; its absence will cause a runtime error. All actual account business logic resides in this sub-program.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '
                   WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'
                   WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '

error_handling.statement: Invalid Menu Choice Handling: If the user enters a digit other than 1–4, the WHEN OTHER clause of the EVALUATE displays an informational error message and returns control to the top of the menu loop. No abend, flag, or logging mechanism is employed for this condition.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN OTHER
                       DISPLAY "Invalid choice, please select 1-4."

error_handling.statement: No ON EXCEPTION / ON OVERFLOW clause is coded on any CALL statement, meaning any failure in loading or executing the 'Operations' sub-program (e.g., program not found, abend) will propagate unhandled and cause a runtime abend with no programmatic recovery.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '
                   WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'
                   WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '

downstream_effects.statement: The 'Operations' sub-program is the sole downstream system affected by this program's execution. Each valid menu selection causes 'Operations' to be invoked with a specific operation code, which may result in account balance reads or mutations, display of account data, and any further downstream effects internal to 'Operations' (e.g., file I/O, database updates). The nature and extent of those effects are defined within 'Operations', not in MainProgram.

code_references.snippet:
WHEN 1
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'TOTAL '
                   WHEN 2
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'CREDIT'
                   WHEN 3
                       CALL 'Operations' USING 'DEBIT '
